title: Self-Service VPC Approval & Audit PRD (sketch)
content: Purpose:\n\nThis is a working PRD sketch for a self-service customer-managed VPC onramp that includes an explicit approval matrix and an audit-log architecture suitable for enterprise customers. The goal is to enable customers to bring their own networking (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, ExpressRoute/Direct Connect equivalents) while preserving Redwood's security posture, meeting audit requirements, and providing predictable operational handoffs for SRE/CS/Customer.
content_continued:
Background and problem statement:

Customers purchasing Private deployments want to maintain networking ownership for compliance or cost reasons. Historically we've handled network handovers manually (ticket-driven, Slack, ad-hoc scripts) which is slow and error-prone for large-scale rollouts. We need a repeatable, auditable flow with automated approval gates, verified connectivity checks, and machine-readable audit logs for evidence and debugging.

Objectives (measurable):
- Reduce manual handoff time from average 3 business days to <4 hours for standard topologies.
- Provide an approval matrix that maps customer actions to Redwood-required gates and roles (SOC, NetOps, Customer Admin).
- Emit audit logs for every approval decision and network lifecycle event with retention options (90/365/730 days).
- Allow CS or the customer's network admin to self-serve common configurations while preserving an operator review step for exceptions.

Scope (in/out):
In scope:
- Self-service VPC registration wizard (CIDR validation, ASN, region, connectivity method).
- Approval gate engine (policy-driven, pluggable) with canary/standard/exception flows.
- Audit logging schema and retention controls surfaced in Console + export hooks (S3, SIEM).
- Automated connectivity validation (BGP reachability, NAT, IP allowlists) and test-run capability.

Out of scope (for this phase):
- Deep automated remediation (we’ll flag, not modify customer infra).
- Full written-runbook handover for custom, multi-vendor SDN appliances.
content_more:
User personas and journeys:
- Customer Network Admin (CNA): registers VPC, provides peering details, responds to approval requests, views audit trail.
- Redwood Platform Engineer (RPE): reviews exceptions, performs final network tests, triggers installation of private agents.
- Customer Success (CS): coordinates timeline, provides customer-facing checklist, escalates to Sales/Legal if needed.

High level flow (happy path):
1) CNA starts onboarding flow in Console -> selects "Bring your own VPC" -> fills in form (CIDR, ASN, peering type, contact).
2) System runs preflight checks (CIDR overlap, public IPs, route table sanity).
3) If preflight passes and matches baseline policy, system schedules an automated connector verification and emits a "standard approval" auto-approve event.
4) Connector verification runs (TCP handshake, BGP session, test request) and emits logs.
5) Once verification completes, Console shows "Connected" and audit entry recorded.
6) If preflight fails policy, flow routes to exceptions queue requiring RPE review; customer sees status and required remediation steps.
content_more2:
Approval matrix (draft):
- Standard: automatic approval if CIDR in allowed-range, ASN match, and dedicated peering method. Roles: System (auto).
- Elevated: requires RPE review when CIDR overlaps with Redwood infra scope or when using transit configurations. Roles: RPE + CNA.
- Legal/security exception: requires SOC sign-off for cross-region data transfer or unusual encryption posture. Roles: SOC + RPE + CNA.

Approval metadata to capture (every approval event must include):
- approver_role (system | rpe | soc | customer-admin)
content_schema_example:
- reason (free text, optionally structured code keys)

Audit log schema (example record):
{
  "event_type": "vpc_onboard",
  "event_id": "evt-20251107-9a1b2c",
  "customer_id": "acct-12345",
  "resource_id": "vpc-67890",
  "action": "approval:standard:auto",
  "actor": "system",
  "actor_id": "system",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-07T16:03:12Z",
  "details": { "cidr": "10.0.0.0/16", "asn": 65123, "region": "us-west-2" },
  "outcome": "success",
  "evidence": [ "bgp-session-verified", "test-http-200" ]
}

Note: the above JSON is illustrative — our persisted event may be in newline-delimited JSON or HEC-compatible format for SIEM ingestion. Audit fields must be sortable and index-friendly (avoid large blobs).
content_retention_and_exports:
Retention and export model (requirements):
- Default retention: 365 days for enterprise customers; options for 90 or 730 day tiers as an account-level setting.
- Export: S3 (customer-managed bucket), Syslog/Splunk/HTTP endpoint (customer SIEM), or Console download (CSV/NDJSON).
- Encryption: logs encrypted at rest with customer keys when Private deployment and KMS is integrated.

Operational concerns and SLOs:
- Approval engine latency: auto-decisions must complete within 30s for standard onramps.
- Verification SLO: connectivity verification must finish within 15 minutes for standard topologies.
- Audit durability: events emitted before any UI state change; if verification fails, system must still emit the failed verification event with error codes.

Security and compliance notes:
- PII in audit logs must be minimized. Do not record customer secret tokens; only record identifiers and hashes where necessary.
- Support for customer-managed KMS for audit logs (bring-your-own-key) in Private deployments.
- Separate access controls: audit log viewer role vs. approval power; RBAC in Console must map to these.

Console UX notes (rough):
- Onboarding page shows stage timeline (submitted -> preflight -> auto-approved -> verification -> connected).
- Each step includes single-click "view audit events" that opens an NDJSON viewer plus direct "export" buttons.
- Exception queue shows required actions and a "request manual review" button with templated justification fields.

Developer / integration surface area (APIs):
- POST /v1/private/vpcs -> submit onboarding request (returns request_id).
- GET /v1/private/vpcs/{request_id}/audit -> paginated NDJSON stream.
- POST /v1/private/vpcs/{request_id}/approve -> internal use for RPE/SOC flows (authenticated via internal tokens).

Open questions (prioritized):
1) What CIDR validation list do we accept for auto-approve? (Product to define default.)
2) What fields are required for legal exceptions vs. technical exceptions? (SOC + Legal).
3) Will customers accept event delivery SLA for exports? (CS validation).
4) Do we implement real-time streaming to customer SIEM or batched export? (engineering tradeoff).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Auto-approve incorrectly marks a risky network as safe -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, require RPE review for any overlapping or ambiguous cases.
- Risk: Audit logs contain sensitive information -> Mitigation: redact and allow BYOK encryption on logs.
content_retention_and_exports_2:
Next steps / immediate action items:
- Align with SOC on the approval matrix and which cases require explicit SOC sign-off (owner: Marta, due 2026-03-20).
- Engineering spike to prototype the preflight checks and an event emitter that writes NDJSON to S3 (owner: Liu, 2w).
- UX mock for onboarding timeline + export buttons (owner: Jordan, 1w).
- Draft a minimal NDJSON schema for legal review and send to Compliance (owner: Asha, 2026-03-17).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a sketch. Looking for feedback on the approval roles and the retention/export primitives. Please add comments inline in Confluence link or ping on #priv-deployments.

Appendix: quick checklist for handover (for CS to use)
- Confirm customer provided correct CIDR and ASN.
- Verify contact person and escalation emails for RPE and SOC.
- Ensure KMS key is provisioned if customer opts for BYOK.
- Schedule maintenance window if any route changes are required.
- Confirm audit export destination and test a sample event.
